addons_available.description: Whether addons can be installed on this instance.

admin_initialized.description: Whether an administrator account already exists. False means the instance is still awaiting its initial setup.

agents.description: Number of standard agents connected to this instance.

edge_agents.description: Number of Edge agents connected to this instance.

instance_id.description: Unique identifier of this Portainer instance.

latest_version.description: Newest Portainer version available upstream, empty when the instance cannot reach the update service.

nodes.description: Total number of nodes across every environment, which is what Portainer licences against.

platform.description: Container platform Portainer itself runs on, such as `docker` or `kubernetes`.

server_edition.description: Portainer edition as the server reports it: `CE`, or `EE` for Business Edition.

server_version.description: Server version reported by the version endpoint. Use it to gate configuration on the Portainer release, for example a resource that needs 2.45 or newer.

update_available.description: Whether a newer Portainer version than the running one is available.

version.description: Version of the running Portainer instance, as reported by its status endpoint.

version_support.description: Support status of the running version, such as `STS` or `LTS`.

name.description: Name of the Portainer tag to look up. The data source will fail if no matching tag is found.
Name of the Portainer team to look up. The data source will fail if no matching team is found.

role.description: Role of the user within the team as returned by Portainer (e.g. team leader, member).

team_id.description: Identifier of the Portainer team the membership belongs to. Combined with user_id to find a specific membership.

user_id.description: Identifier of the Portainer user whose membership in the team is being looked up.

leader_user_ids.description: Identifiers of the team's leaders, who may manage its membership.

team_id.description: Identifier of the team whose members are listed.

created_authentication_method.description: Authentication method used when the user was created (Portainer 3.0+). One of `internal`, `ldap` or `oauth` (Portainer `portainer.AuthenticationMethod` 1/2/3). Empty on Portainer releases before 3.0, which do not report it, and when the server has not recorded it.

last_authentication_method.description: Authentication method used at the user's last login (Portainer 3.0+). One of `internal`, `ldap` or `oauth` (Portainer `portainer.AuthenticationMethod` 1/2/3). Empty on Portainer releases before 3.0, which do not report it, and when the server has not recorded it.

role.description: Role assigned to the user in Portainer: 1 = admin, 2 = user.

username.description: Username of the Portainer user to look up. The data source will fail if no matching user is found.

effective_access.description: Access the user effectively has on every environment, with the policy each entry comes from. This is the resolved result of user policies, team policies and group inheritance — the answer to "why can this person see that environment".

role.description: Portainer role of the user: 1 = administrator, 2 = standard user.

user_id.description: Identifier of the user to inspect. Leave unset to describe the user the provider authenticates as.

username.description: Username of the inspected user.

activity_logs.description: List of user activity log entries returned by Portainer when `log_type` is set to `activity`.

after.description: Return results after this unix timestamp.

auth_logs.description: List of authentication log entries returned by Portainer when `log_type` is set to `auth`.

before.description: Return results before this unix timestamp.

context.description: Filter by context (only for activity logs).

log_type.description: Type of logs to retrieve: 'activity' for user activity logs, 'auth' for authentication logs.

total_count.description: Total count of matching logs (only for activity logs).

username.description: Filter by usernames (only for activity logs).

namespaces.description: The user's namespace authorizations, one entry per environment and namespace.

raw.description: The whole response as Portainer returns it, encoded as JSON. Portainer adds authorization names between releases, so this is what to read when a name is not in the flattened list yet.

user_id.description: Identifier of the user whose namespace authorizations are read.

endpoint_id.description: Identifier of the Portainer environment (endpoint) where the webhook is registered.

resource_id.description: Identifier of the resource (e.g. service) the Portainer webhook is attached to. Combined with endpoint_id to find the webhook.

token.description: Token used to invoke the Portainer webhook URL.

webhook_type.description: Type of the Portainer webhook (e.g. service webhook, container webhook).
